segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: Morning, this is planning for sprint 14. Two weeks, ending on the 20th.

segments.speaker: Ritika Saxena
segments.text: Morning. Quick heads up, I'm out Wednesday to Friday next week for a family wedding.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: Thanks, I'll factor that in. Let's look at what's on top of the backlog.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: The two big ones are group bookings and dark mode.

segments.speaker: Daniel Thomas
segments.text: Group bookings is the one the sales people keep asking about.

segments.speaker: Meenal Desai
segments.text: Dark mode has been sitting in the backlog for three sprints now.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: I know. But the hotel partners need group bookings before the holiday season.

segments.speaker: Ritika Saxena
segments.text: Doing both in one sprint with me out three days won't happen.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: Then the sprint goal is group bookings. Dark mode moves to sprint 15.

segments.speaker: Meenal Desai
segments.text: Okay, as long as it actually happens in 15.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: It's first in line for 15, I promise.

segments.speaker: Daniel Thomas
segments.text: For group bookings, the API has to come first. Frontend can't do much without it.

segments.speaker: Ritika Saxena
segments.text: I can build the screens against a mock while you finish it.

segments.speaker: Daniel Thomas
segments.text: The API contract is mostly done. I'll finish the group booking API by Wednesday.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: Great, that gives Ritika most of the sprint for the screens.

segments.speaker: Meenal Desai
segments.text: I'll need time for testing. Group bookings have a lot of edge cases, partial cancellations and so on.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: Meenal, can you have the test cases written by the end of next week?

segments.speaker: Meenal Desai
segments.text: Yes, test cases for group bookings by the end of next week.

segments.speaker: Daniel Thomas
segments.text: Remember the client demo is on 24 November, so the build should be stable by then.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: Good point, but the demo is a separate track, sales handles that.

segments.speaker: Ritika Saxena
segments.text: Points. How much are we taking in?

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: We usually do around 40, but with Ritika out I'd cap it.

segments.speaker: Daniel Thomas
segments.text: 34 sounds right to me.

segments.speaker: Ritika Saxena
segments.text: 34 is fine. I'd rather finish than carry over.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: Then we cap this sprint at 34 points.

segments.speaker: Daniel Thomas
segments.text: Can I raise something? Two-week sprints feel too long. What about one-week sprints?

segments.speaker: Meenal Desai
segments.text: One-week sprints would double the planning overhead for QA.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: And we'd change process in the middle of the holiday rush. Not now.

segments.speaker: Daniel Thomas
segments.text: Okay, I'll drop it, but I want to revisit it in January.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: Noted for the retro, nothing changes for now.

segments.speaker: Meenal Desai
segments.text: Something that's hurting me, the checkout tests are flaky again.

segments.speaker: Ritika Saxena
segments.text: They failed twice on my branch yesterday for no reason.

segments.speaker: Daniel Thomas
segments.text: It's the timing on the payment mock, I think. It's been there for months.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: We need someone to look into the flaky checkout tests this sprint.

segments.speaker: Daniel Thomas
segments.text: I'm on the API, so not me.

segments.speaker: Ritika Saxena
segments.text: And I'm out three days, so I can't promise.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: Okay, I'll put the ticket in the sprint unassigned and we'll pick it up at stand-up.

segments.speaker: Meenal Desai
segments.text: Fine, but please let's not ignore it again.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: Bug count. We have six open from last sprint.

segments.speaker: Daniel Thomas
segments.text: Four of those are cosmetic, the other two are in the booking flow.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: The two booking bugs go into this sprint, the cosmetic ones wait.

segments.speaker: Ritika Saxena
segments.text: One of the cosmetic ones is the misaligned button on the profile page. It's a ten minute fix.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: If it's ten minutes, just do it, no ticket drama.

segments.speaker: Meenal Desai
segments.text: What about the release? Do we release at the end of the sprint?

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: Yes, release on the last Friday as usual, if QA signs off.

segments.speaker: Daniel Thomas
segments.text: Do we have a staging slot that week? The other team was using it.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: I'll check with them, I think they're done by then.

segments.speaker: Ritika Saxena
segments.text: Can someone share the design file for the group booking screens? I only have the old version.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: I'll forward the latest file after this call.

segments.speaker: Meenal Desai
segments.text: Okay, I think that's the plan.

segments.speaker: Ishaan Chawla
segments.text: Great. Thanks everyone, good sprint.

decisions.fact: The sprint 14 goal is group bookings; dark mode moves to sprint 15.
Sprint 14 is capped at 34 story points.

action_items.fact: Daniel finishes the group booking API.
Meenal writes the test cases for group bookings.
action_items.due_phrase: by the end of next week

action_items.fact: The flaky checkout tests get investigated this sprint; nobody took it.

distractors.fact: Moving to one-week sprints was suggested and dropped.
24 November is the client demo, not the test cases' due date.
